title: Flowdia
subtitle: Multi-agent application platform
description: A platform where a team of specialised AI agents plans, designs, builds and ships production web apps end to end, each with a real backend, a dedicated PostgreSQL database and APIs. I build the agent orchestration and LLM integration layer, and the system that turns natural-language product intent into deployed applications with memory that persists across sessions.

title: GitHub Projects
subtitle: Planning and tracking, at GitHub scale
description: The planning and tracking experience used by organisations and developers worldwide. I shipped saved views, user-owned projects, the project GraphQL APIs, fast issues, the iterations field and the issue sidebar — inside the github/github monolith, alongside large-scale performance work and distributed data migrations across hundreds of millions of records.

title: Bardy
subtitle: Visual feedback and collaboration
description: Comment directly on live websites, videos, PDFs and images, edit HTML and CSS in place, and capture screenshots automatically — delivered as a web app and a Chrome extension on a multi-tenant SaaS. Built end to end as one of two co-founders. We wound the company down in late 2025 when traction did not materialise.

title: Grow Healthy
subtitle: Healthcare logistics platform
description: Led the frontend and backend teams building and deploying a healthcare delivery platform. Order processing ran on Firestore, Scheduler, Pub/Sub and Cloud Functions, with Twilio, OnFleet, Zendesk and Google Maps integrated, Jest unit and end-to-end coverage, and automated deployments through GitHub Actions.

title: WiPi
subtitle: Remotely-accessible wireless testbed
description: A low-cost, large-scale, heterogeneous wireless network testbed that researchers could access remotely to run next-generation network experiments. The core of my doctoral work, published in IEEE Access and presented at IEEE VTC.

title: This site
subtitle: A CV you can ask questions
description: Statically exported to GitHub Pages, with a serverless API on Vercel that proxies OpenRouter so the key never reaches the browser. MongoDB enforces per-visitor and site-wide rate limits, and every answer is grounded strictly in this CV — if something is not in it, the assistant says so rather than inventing it.
